content: Level 3 hypoglycemia, as defined by the American Diabetes Association (ADA), is classified as severe hypoglycemia. This condition is marked by significant cognitive impairment, which may manifest as confusion, inability to concentrate, or disorientation. It is also associated with physical symptoms that can include weakness, dizziness, or loss of motor coordination. In such cases, the individual often requires external assistance to recover, as they may be unable to self-manage their condition. If left untreated, severe hypoglycemia can result in serious complications, including loss of consciousness, seizures, or even death.
